attempts.url: AWS publishes no OpenAPI document for S3; its own machine spec is the SDK service model

attempts.note: AWS's own service model — the true upstream, but converting it needs an aws2openapi-equivalent this repo does not have yet
apis.guru's aws2openapi rendering of that AWS model

notes: Full coverage of the Amazon S3 REST API — 97 operations over 49 paths (query-string variants disambiguated with a # fragment) and 574 component schemas: objects, multipart uploads, buckets, ACLs, policies, CORS, encryption, lifecycle, replication, tagging, versioning, inventory, analytics, object lock and S3 Select. Replaces a 5 KiB spec synthesized from the adaptor's three operations (put/list/get), all three of which are present here. PROVENANCE, per the vendor-published-only rule: AWS hosts no OpenAPI document. Its own machine spec is the SDK service model (aws-sdk-js apis/s3-2006-03-01.normal.json); upstream.json is apis.guru's aws2openapi rendering of that model, which is the only OpenAPI form published anywhere — hence origin=converted, not found-openapi. BEST-EFFORT: the rendering covers S3 through roughly 2021 (GetObjectAttributes and WriteGetObjectResponse are in; the 2023+ S3 Express operations CreateSession/ListDirectoryBuckets and the bucket metadata-configuration operations are not). Converting AWS's model directly would close that gap and is the obvious follow-up.
